verdicts.marker_line: String helpers 1.0.0: inert tarball; hostile repo hooks absent
Wednesday Wallpaper 2.61: UI searches; fix authority/XSS claims
Atom's Connections 1.7.1: peer chat; no covert collection found

analysis_method: Static only. Original SHA-256s verified; every provided archive member compared byte-for-byte to extracted files. atomscan slow/no-update/follow=none and cleave facts ran for each original. Referenced code and data were separately fetched with forager, retaining provenance in scratch. Only inspected pure string decoders and lookup/rotation/arithmetic wrappers were evaluated in a time-limited isolated QuickJS context; no sample entry point was executed.

evidence: Exactly three files: manifest, README, and 582-byte index.js. Four exported helpers capitalize, truncate, camelToKebab, and countWords perform string transformations only.
No lifecycle scripts, dependencies, dynamic evaluation, process execution, filesystem access, or network calls in the tarball.

Current linked repository differs from these original release bytes despite still declaring version 1.0.0. It includes .github/init.js and Claude/Gemini SessionStart hooks, Cursor MCP/rules, VS Code folder-open task, and a test script that launches the loader. Those files and hooks are absent from the tarball.

Recovered repository loader through numeric-character conversion, ROT10, AES-128-GCM and Brotli. Decoded 15,444 string-table calls plus 873 PBKDF2/SHA256/permutation-encrypted strings. Its Bun payload collects developer/cloud/application credentials, discovers tokens, reads cloud secret services, exports encrypted results through GitHub/GitLab senders and attempts repository/package propagation. The fetched repository is hostile; it is not an executed dependency of this inert archive.
samples.source_label_explanation: The referenced repository supplies concrete malicious context and could explain package-name/campaign-based labeling. It does not establish an activation path in these exact tarball bytes. The registry sidecar also records a fresh, removed release. BENIGN applies only to this artifact; it should not establish trust in the repository or other releases.
samples.trait_changes: None to the original package; all original detections retained.

samples.identification: Wednesday Live Wallpapers New Tab 2.61, Gameograf
evidence: MV3 replaces the new tab; search, alarms and storage are declared. Host authority is restricted to api.gameograf.com; no all-site content scripts, history/cookie permission, default-search override or network redirect rules.
Install callback opens one marketing tab only for reason=install. Startup and a 30-minute alarm refresh promotion/shortcut JSON and flush aggregate tab counts. Uninstall navigates to a publisher URL.

Search button/Enter dispatches chrome.search.query using the typed query; the worker contains no search call. No IndexedDB deletion, native payload, credential collection or victim-page interception was found.

Tracking POSTs contain aggregate tab count or banner event/timestamp, two-letter UI language and extension ID. Weather supports automatic server-side location and optional user-entered city. These are observable network/telemetry capabilities, retained at notable severity.

Fetched current message/shortcut responses contain publisher promotions and ordinary site links, without an executable breakout. Banner text uses textContent and can be disabled; shortcut fields still enter jQuery-generated HTML without full escaping. This is a real rendering surface, not evidence that a hostile payload was delivered.

Bundled jQuery is byte-identical to official 3.7.1. The outside-batch pelenccnijhcgalnjgaddejabgafpble 4 sample was fetched by SHA-256; it independently exhibits the same benign worker-refresh/user-search split.
samples.source_label_explanation: Unit 42 documents publisher-level adware, forced affiliate traffic and other builds containing IndexedDB deletion/HTML popups. The supplied 2.61 code has promotion/telemetry but lacks those destructive or coercive paths. Reputation alone does not supply them.

samples.identification: Atom's Connections 1.7.1 beta, Ultra Encode, LLC
evidence: Traced all 17 CLR methods. Entry Main -> Run -> loopback HttpListener on 127.0.0.1/localhost:47800, then opens that URL using ProcessStartInfo.UseShellExecute. No native payload or assembly activation path.

LoadFiles checks app.pak SHA-256 db2fd6b4dc620bdddf8cad94e451514066e9cd8181f40ba9a4905159800ccc3c, gzip-decompresses it, and parses length-prefixed assets into memory: index.html 616829 bytes, player.html 5019 bytes, vendor/peerjs.min.js 92865 bytes.

Generated 32-byte device key uses DPAPI CurrentUser; it protects this application’s encrypted vault. Host and cross-site checks protect sensitive loopback routes; /device-key and /save require POST and X-Atoms:1. SafeTarget bounds save paths to application Pictures/Documents roots and rejects traversal/device names.

EndOtherCopies queries the current executable basename via WMI and checks the configured port before terminating another instance. Protocol registration writes only HKCU Software\Classes\atoms with quoted own-path/%1. Desktop shortcut creation is visible; neither is an autorun trigger.

Decoded 10979 constant decoder calls in main UI and 83 in the player. Received peer identity is checked against its public key; static/ephemeral ECDH, HKDF and AES-GCM protect sessions and sequence counters reject replays. Invitations/contact/session checks gate peer data handlers. Recovered dispatch covers messaging, posts, selected media, groups, games and calls; no covert collection or shell dispatch found.

Updater validates same-origin download metadata and offers a user-clicked download; it does not execute installers. Plugin packages are hash-checked and mounted in allow-scripts-only sandbox frames with connect-src/frame-src none and per-plugin permissions.

Bundled PeerJS is byte-identical to upstream 1.5.4, SHA-256 ad5d8870d1e389914f9cba8d35be313c4327c69ee0a221e482e9bf7621136fe5. Current site version JSON advertises 1.11.0, corroborating product identity but not authenticating 1.7.1. Downloaded Math Lab/Neon Arcade plugins match current catalog hashes and contain game functionality.
samples.packaging_and_context: No Authenticode security directory/signature, no strong-name signature, no PE overlay; asInvoker manifest. Embedded resource digest is integrity-only, not publisher authentication. No installer, supplied invitation, provisioned attacker peer, command line or host execution history was provided. A specific deployment could be abused; that context is missing.
samples.source_label_explanation: 31/71 external engines and malware-corpus provenance are retained as leads. Unsigned high-entropy compressed assets, extensive JS obfuscation, DPAPI, WMI termination, COM and network references plausibly trigger heuristics. The actual collection reason is unknown; no hostile deployment was invented.
samples.trait_changes: No changes to PE detections; every original finding remains.

rule_changes.reason: Required evidence was manifest declarations, never periodic search execution. A detached manifest does not add behavior. Corrected name, placement, notable severity and unsupported T1176 mapping; all actual grants remain visible. New profile omits the exact host predicate, since hostname identity is independently engine-emitted and is not needed to describe alarm/storage/search declarations.
Unchanged declaration matcher and notable severity; authority belongs in permission metadata rather than unwanted product identity. Updated focused fixture consumer.
Duplicate static host-grant finding removed; canonical engine finding remains notable on the same manifest and archive.

Matcher also accepts ordinary dollar-call selector templates and does not require HTML. Preserved matcher, scopes and notable severity; source call syntax placement and precise description replace the unsupported HTML-parsing/exploit implication. Updated the exact composite consumer; removed inherited unsupported T1189/T1059.007/E1059 mappings.

reference_audit: No active ancestor-directory consumers of the removed Gameograf leaf/unwanted root, old remote-feed-xss ancestors, or new source/permission leaves were found. Exact Gameograf fixture reference and exact XSS composite reference updated. No behavioral suppressor was added.
verification: All original files and archive members compared before/after under the explicit ID mappings; no supported observation lost. Final originals have zero suspicious/hostile findings.
4 authority controls and 2 HTML/selector source controls passed.
Outside-batch Gameograf CRX retains all supported observations after mapping.
Existing global-link-click-hijack XPI retains hostile interception and suspicious forwarding detections.
Staged existing inline-breakout/script-loader controls still fire hostile JSON/markup payload and script-loader detections after the source-atom move.
material_detection_losses: Only unsupported periodic-background-search severity/claim and the duplicate grant finding were removed. Exact template matching and its attack consumer remain. No verified attack detection lost.
remaining_gaps: Original PE scan does not recursively expose the custom gzip/length-prefixed CLR web assets. Their JS obfuscation, WebRTC and browser cryptography required manual extraction; an entropy-based hostile rule would not repair this engine gap.
JavaScript scans record limited/incomplete value-flow facts. Manual source tracing supplied the execution and data-flow evidence above.

Model bundle is feature spec v18 while extractor expects v19; atomscan warns new features are zero-filled. All three original scans remain off the calibrated alert grid (level -1); raw probabilities are recorded separately. External source labels remain in disagreement with these artifact-specific BENIGN judgments.
